globalNotes: Both Yoast and Rank Math postmeta exist in the export. Yoast is the populated set (_yoast_wpseo_metadesc on 241 of 263 posts); Rank Math meta is sparse (rank_math_title on 20, rank_math_description on 82) and is a partial migration artifact. Rank Math is what runs on live, so nothing in the export maps 1:1 to the live plugin.

NO canonical URL is set anywhere in the export: neither _yoast_wpseo_canonical nor rank_math_canonical_url appears on any of the 263 posts. Every legacy article relied on the implicit self-canonical. This is a source fact, not a per-article defect.

76 of the 163 have a Yoast SEO title that is only a template variable (%%title%%, %%title%% %%page%%, %%title%% %%sep%%, %title%). These carry no editorial value and must not be imported as literal titles; 23 more have no SEO title at all. Only 64 of 163 have a real hand-written SEO title.

wp_schema_pro_optimized_structured_data is present on all 163 as a frozen JSON-LD blob. 13 of them carry @id URLs under the dead WPML locale prefixes https://gcalls.co/en/ (7) and https://gcalls.co/ja/ (6), so the structured data pointed at URLs that no longer exist even on the old site. @type is NewsArticle, which is wrong for evergreen how-to content.
29 of the 163 carry _yoast_post_redirect_info, meaning the legacy URL already had a redirect rule configured on the old site; those rules are not in the repo redirect manifest.
33 articles carry 36 _wp_old_slug values. Those are additional legacy URLs that once resolved and should be included as aliases in any redirect work.

Articles resolve at root level (/<slug>/), the same shape as gcalls.co, so the 37 page slugs share one namespace with all article slugs. No collision exists today, but the namespace is flat and unguarded.
